transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (Lodestar Head of Eng), Ethan Mills (Lodestar Security Eng), Priya Rao (PM)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/decks/data-retention (deck), https://redwood.app/docs/kms-integration, benchmark sheet: https://sheets.redwood/lodestar-bench (view only)

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through our data handling and retention controls, show you the Console toggles, how request storage and redaction works, and then Samir will run a quick live demo of the API behavior.
[00:18] Maria: thanks Avery, quick note - we care a lot about PII redaction and not storing cardholder data; also need KMS integration and audit log evidence for our audit in Q1.
[00:30] Avery: got it, that's what we planned to cover. samir, quick intro?
[00:35] Samir: yeah hi all, Samir here, I'm the SE on the account — technical deep dives are my favorite, we'll show both Console and API flows, plus the Optimize recommendations for batching vs retention tradeoffs.
[00:50] Priya: timeline for pilot? we said Jan pilot ideally.
[00:55] Avery: yep pilot target week of Jan 4, we'll confirm after the benchmark.
[01:10] Samir: ok starting with the Console — login screen, top-level policy page; so you can choose global retention policy, and then per-route overrides. for example you can toggle request storage off entirely for a route that handles payment tokens.
[01:30] Ethan: curious, when storage is toggled off does that stop all logs or only request/response payloads?
[01:38] Samir: good question — toggling request storage off disables persistent storage of request and response bodies; metadata like request size, latency, and status codes are still captured for observability and billing unless you enable additional suppressions. note, audit logs (who changed policy) are always retained for compliance with retention windows configured by the org.
[01:58] Maria: and where are request bodies stored when enabled, like region and residency?
[02:05] Samir: stored in the same region as your tenant by default; for Private deployments you control the storage endpoints. for Hosted customers we have region selection and data residency guarantees — we can add a residency clause in the contract.
[02:20] Avery: also covered is KMS — we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) so at-rest encryption keys are under customer control.
[02:30] Ethan: can you rotate keys without downtime?
[02:33] Samir: yes, key rotation is supported via a rewrapping flow; no inference downtime, but a short rewrapping job may increase backend CPU briefly. we'll share the KMS integration docs.
[02:45] Priya: show us redaction in action?
[02:48] Samir: sure — switching to the live API demo. I'm going to send three sample requests: one normal, one with an email and cc last4, and one with a JSON payload that includes a social_security_number field.
[03:05] [03:05] Samir: POST /v1/generate ... ok first request, response back quick. this one is stored because the route has storage enabled.
[03:20] Maria: can you show the Console view where you see the raw request?
[03:24] Samir: sure, here in the Console under Request Log you can click into the event and see the raw payload if storage is enabled. but we recommend enabling redaction rules to mask PII before writing to disk.
[03:35] [03:35] Samir: now I toggle the route-level redaction policy — redact by JSON path: $.user.email and $.payment.card_number, also a regex for SSN patterns.
[03:50] Ethan: regex can be dangerous, any false positives we should worry about?
[03:54] Samir: yep it's best to combine JSON path + type checks; our Console gives a simulator so you can paste a sample payload and it will show how the rule transforms it before commit.
[04:10] Priya: that simulator will be helpful for our product folks.
[04:15] Samir: demoing simulator now — pasted the SSN payload and you can see the output shows "REDACTED_SSN" and email as "***@example.com". note the simulator is client-side and doesn't change stored data until you apply.
[04:30] Maria: what about function-calling / tool-calls — if we call external tools, do those transcripts get stored?
[04:38] Samir: by default function payloads are treated like request bodies; route-level toggles apply. you can also set per-tool storage policies, e.g., allow tool X to log but not store full payloads.
[04:50] [04:50] Avery: question around PII discovery — do you have an automated discovery engine or is it rule-based?
[04:58] Samir: both — we have pattern detectors for common PII and a rules engine for JSON path and regex. automated discovery flags probable PII and suggests rules; you still confirm before rules are applied.
[05:12] Ethan: for our compliance we need tamper-evident audit logs and SSO + RBAC.
[05:18] Samir: we have audit logs, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. audit logs are immutable and can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or cloud storage export.
[05:32] Priya: ok what about data retention default windows?
[05:36] Samir: defaults are 30 days for request bodies and 365 days for audit logs, but you can set global defaults and per-route overrides; for Dedicated/Private we can commit to custom retention SLAs.
[05:50] Maria: are there hard deletes? like if we need to remove all traces for a customer record?
[05:55] Samir: we support point-in-time deletion for stored requests matching a given id or selector; for full account deletion we have a purge workflow that removes objects and rotates keys and emits a deletion certificate. note that backups may retain copies for a short TTL depending on backup policies — we include that in the deletion certificate specifics.
[06:20] [06:20] Samir: switching back to Console UI — now showing the tenant-level configs, policy inheritance, and the Optimize panel. Optimize suggests where to enable prefix caching and where to disable storing requests to save costs while keeping latency SLOs intact.
[06:40] Maria: can Optimize quantify cost savings?
[06:43] Samir: yes it provides an estimated cost delta and latency impact per suggestion, e.g., disabling request storage for high-volume low-trace routes could reduce storage costs by ~60% for that workload.
[06:58] Priya: we run heavy embedding workloads too; how does retention apply for embeddings?
[07:04] Samir: embeddings are stored separately; you can set retention per-index and optionally enable automatic pruning or TTL on vectors. for PCI-sensitive vector payloads we recommend not storing the raw text and using hashed references.
[07:20] Ethan: about PCI — is Redwood PCI-compliant or do we need Dedicated?
[07:25] Samir: Redwood Hosted is not PCI-certified by default; customers processing cardholder data typically use Dedicated or Private with our compliance package and controls that meet PCI requirements. we can scope a compliance plan.
[07:40] Maria: ok this is important for us.
[07:42] Avery: we'll include the Dedicated pricing and the compliance add-on in the follow-up.
[07:48] [07:48] Samir: now I'm going to demonstrate API-level toggles: there's a request header you can pass to mark requests as 'no-store' which enforces ephemeral mode for that request regardless of route defaults — useful for tokens or sensitive single requests.
[08:05] Priya: does 'no-store' affect billing or analytics?
[08:09] Samir: billing metrics still count tokens and request counts for invoicing; analytics like latency still aggregate, but payloads aren't stored. we can also anonymize telemetry further if you want token-level obfuscation.
[08:25] Maria: do you have sample code for integrating the no-store header into our gateway?
[08:29] Samir: yep we'll share the snippet in the repo and the test harness.
[08:36] [08:36] Samir: demoing the no-store header now, sending a request with X-Redwood-No-Store: true — request appears in logs transiently but no raw body persists in the Console.
[08:50] Ethan: regarding encryption at rest - you mentioned CMEK, but do you support HSM-backed keys?
[08:56] Samir: yes for Private deployments we can integrate with HSMs and FIPS-140 validated modules; for Hosted we support cloud KMS providers.
[09:08] Priya: any limits on retention granularity? like minutes/hours?
[09:12] Samir: retention is expressed in days; the smallest granularity in the UI is 1 day, but via API you can set TTL in seconds for private infra.
[09:24] Maria: we also need exportability for legal e-discovery. can you export raw payloads (if stored) to an S3 bucket?
[09:32] Samir: yes, exports to customer buckets with encryption are supported; export requests generate an audit event and can be scoped by time range, route, or selector.
[09:44] [09:44] Priya: what about consent and data subject requests?
[09:47] Samir: we have a DSAR workflow — you can run a selector to find all requests related to an identifier and either redact or delete them; there's an audit trail for the DSAR.
[09:58] Maria: any gotchas for our stack? we run a hybrid infra with GCP primary and Azure for DR.
[10:05] Samir: region failover is supported; for multi-cloud residency we can deploy Private nodes in both clouds or use Dedicated with cross-region replication policies.
[10:18] Avery: quick callout — competitors like BigCloudAI advertise similar toggles but usually lack the per-route simulator and certificate deletion workflows. mention InferEdge as also pushing on-prem solutions.
[10:33] Maria: good to know.
[10:36] [10:36] Samir: moving to the redaction logs — Console keeps a redaction log showing original hash + redacted value mapping, salted per-tenant so you can prove redaction happened without revealing raw PII.
[10:50] Ethan: can we bring our own hashing salt?
[10:53] Samir: yes with Private/Dedicated we support customer-provided salts and HMAC keys.
[11:02] Priya: that helps.
[11:05] [11:05] Samir: next I'll run a small benchmark to show the cost/latency delta when disabling request storage for a high-throughput route. sending a 1000 req/sec synthetic for 30s.
[11:20] [11:20] Samir: results are in — 99th pctl latency increased by 20ms when storage was enabled due to write amplification; disabling storage reduces tail latency and lowers cost. estimate numbers are in the benchmark sheet I shared.
[11:38] Maria: can you produce a benchmark run against our sample dataset?
[11:42] Samir: yes, that's part of the pilot — we'll run the benchmark on your data with your retention policies, request shapes, and network topology.
[11:52] Avery: action items and next steps i'll recap at the end.
[12:00] [12:00] Priya: one more question — do you offer per-tenant redaction rule versioning? we may need to roll back a rule.
[12:07] Samir: yes rules are versioned and you can preview previous versions in the Console and rollback.
[12:15] Ethan: for SIEM integration, what fields are included in audit exports?
[12:19] Samir: exports include event, timestamp, principal, action, route, and a pointer to the object id; they do not include raw payloads unless you opt-in to include them.
[12:32] [12:32] Maria: ok thanks, this is helpful.
[12:35] Avery: final recap — we'll send SOC2 + KMS docs (Avery), Samir will schedule the Lodestar-specific benchmark and share test plan (Samir), Priya will supply sample payloads and redaction rules (Priya). We'll aim for a pilot the week of 2027-01-04.
[12:55] Maria: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
